answer: Proof-of-work admission: each new identity must solve a costly hash puzzle before it can earn or grade. Picture the trust graph as a grove where every vertex pays its own entry fee. An honest agent pays once, but a Sybil farm of 10,000 fake vertices pays 10,000 times, so the attacker climbs a cost ridge that grows linearly with the attack while rewards per identity stay capped. If admission costs more compute than a new identity can earn before it is established, faking identities loses money.
